images.title: Evidence Readiness by Research Question
images.what_it_shows: A stacked count of available, partial, and needed evidence for each research question.
images.expected_metrics: Each RQ should move toward more Available items and fewer Needed/Partial items before the thesis makes strong claims.
images.interpretation: RQ2 and RQ3 are critical because their missing validation and ClimateBERT comparison work directly determine whether the ABSA results are defensible.
images.if_underperforming: If a row remains dominated by Needed or Partial evidence, the RQ should be presented as preliminary or narrowed until the missing metric is computed.

images.title: Overall Evidence Status Totals
images.what_it_shows: The total count of evidence rows by status across the whole RQ evidence matrix.
images.expected_metrics: A mature thesis evidence set should have most rows Available, with only low-priority items remaining Partial or Needed.
images.interpretation: This chart is a readiness check, not a statistical test. It tells you how much of the evidence pipeline has been completed.
images.if_underperforming: Large Partial/Needed counts mean the dashboard should redirect users to processing, annotation, or validation workflows.

images.title: RQ Priority and Evidence Gap Matrix
images.what_it_shows: A compact table image linking RQ priority to the amount of available, partial, and needed evidence.
images.expected_metrics: Critical and High RQs should have direct metrics, traceable sources, and low unclosed Needed counts.
images.interpretation: The most important risk is not simply the number of gaps; it is whether a gap belongs to a Critical RQ.
images.if_underperforming: If a Critical RQ has Needed rows, the page should route the user to the processor, result visualizer, annotation plan, or parsed-data page.

images.title: Sample Size Reasoning Ladder
images.what_it_shows: A practical ladder of sample sizes and what each size can support in the thesis.
images.expected_metrics: Manual validation usually needs at least 30-50 records; subgroup comparisons need substantially more balanced rows.
images.interpretation: Current row counts can support descriptive analysis, but smaller slices by language, pillar, prompt, or model may still be fragile.
images.if_underperforming: If a subgroup has too few rows, report it as exploratory and avoid strong comparative claims.

images.title: Approximate Margin of Error by Sample Size
images.what_it_shows: How uncertainty shrinks as the number of validated rows grows.
images.expected_metrics: For proportion estimates such as tone rate, more rows reduce uncertainty; n=272 gives roughly +/-5.9 percentage points in the worst case.
images.interpretation: The thesis can report descriptive proportions, but subgroup results need enough rows per subgroup, not just a large total row count.
images.if_underperforming: If a subgroup is below n=30-50, use it for qualitative diagnostics rather than quantitative claims.

images.title: Subgroup Coverage Requirement Check
images.what_it_shows: The row counts needed when validation is split by language, pillar, model, or prompt.
images.expected_metrics: A useful target is 30-50 validated rows per important subgroup.
images.interpretation: This chart explains why some RQ evidence remains Partial even when the dataset already has many rows.
images.if_underperforming: If important cells are sparse, add data or collapse categories before claiming subgroup differences.

images.title: Workflow Diagram
images.what_it_shows: The operational pipeline connecting source reports, parsed records, ClimateBERT processing, prediction outputs, and the RQ evidence page.
images.expected_metrics: Every output should be traceable back to data_output.txt or climatebert_predictions, with page-level or row-level provenance where possible.
images.interpretation: The dashboard should treat page 02 as the production step, page 03 as the prediction review step, and page 04 as the thesis-evidence interpretation layer.
images.if_underperforming: If any handoff is missing, the downstream chart may still render but it will be hard to audit or continue after interruption.

images.title: Missing Evidence Process
images.what_it_shows: The completion workflow for rows marked Needed or Partial in the RQ details table.
images.expected_metrics: Each missing item should name a source, a process, and a metric that can be computed and added back to the evidence table.
images.interpretation: Needed rows are not errors. They are explicit thesis work items with a destination page and completion metric.
images.if_underperforming: If a Needed row has no route or metric, it should be rewritten until the next action is executable.

images.title: Full Research Question Evidence Map
images.what_it_shows: A high-level lineage map from source artifacts to the six research questions.
images.expected_metrics: Each RQ should be linked to the data source that supports it and the status counts that indicate readiness.
images.interpretation: RQ3 depends most directly on prediction outputs, while RQ2 and RQ4 also need expert annotation to become fully defensible.
images.if_underperforming: If a source-to-RQ link is weak or missing, the RQ should not be presented as fully supported yet.

research_question_explanations.question: How can a PDF-to-structured ESG transformation pipeline convert Indonesian/English sustainability reports into a governance-aligned, sentence-level representation that supports ABSA?
available_evidence: PDF sustainability reports: 6 docs available; BEST, VKTR, GTRA, PTBA, ICR, Indonet
Markdown page outputs from OCR pipeline with source-page traceability
Records-per-run throughput: mean 8.5 records/run; Arcee 14.3 records/run
Field completion: 100% aspect/ESG/tone; 81.3% sentiment_score
partial_evidence: JSON extraction records with provenance: 332 records
needed_evidence: ESG topic alignment accuracy from manual verification
research_question_explanations.interpretation: Pipeline evidence is strong for parsing and traceability, but OCR and sentence-boundary quality still need direct measurement.

research_question_explanations.question: How should ESG be categorized by aspect/pillar, sentiment, and tone in bilingual disclosures to enable fine-grained ABSA while preserving cross-language comparability?
available_evidence: Tone x ESG pillar cross-tabulation: E commitment=91, G commitment=24, S commitment=0
Bilingual tone asymmetry: Indonesian outcome 7.9% vs English 21.8%
Sentiment score distribution by tone: outcome mean=0.60 vs commitment mean=0.03
partial_evidence: LLM labels: 332 records; commitment=115, action=58, outcome=50
needed_evidence: Expert-annotated ground truth corpus: 30-50 records, 2 annotators
research_question_explanations.interpretation: Categorization has useful descriptive distributions, but gold labels and inter-annotator agreement are required before treating labels as validated ABSA.

research_question_explanations.question: Do tone-based ABSA outputs differ meaningfully from ClimateBERT-style label classifications, and what is the relationship between detected tone and climate-specific targets?
available_evidence: LLM-assigned ClimateBERT-style label families: 16 label families
Co-occurrence frequency: commitment + climate-commitment = 91
partial_evidence: Tone x ClimateBERT label crosstab exists, but labels are LLM-assigned
Missing tone vs CB label analysis identifies possible false negatives
needed_evidence: ClimateBERT scores for all valid records from local runs
Row-wise agreement between tone and ClimateBERT labels
Cohen kappa between LLM tone and ClimateBERT classification

metrics.note: far too few; must run locally

research_question_explanations.interpretation: ClimateBERT comparison becomes defensible only when local model prediction CSVs cover all valid records and can be joined back to the parsed dataset.

research_question_explanations.question: What weaknesses arise in ABSA extraction outputs, and how can a diagnostics framework detect and quantify extraction errors to inform model improvement?
available_evidence: Complete extraction log per run
Schema drift records: 18 records from data.md + GPT-oss-120b
Missing tone records with context: 61 records
Root cause attribution by model x prompt
Schema drift rate by prompt template
partial_evidence: Non-standard aspect labels: 41 unique free-text Indonesian labels
needed_evidence: Formal error taxonomy: wrong-aspect, wrong-tone, wrong-pillar, schema-failure, OCR-noise
research_question_explanations.interpretation: Diagnostics are already useful for identifying schema drift and missing tone, but manual error labels are needed for a formal error taxonomy.

research_question_explanations.question: What is the stability of ABSA outputs across cross-model and cross-prompt configurations, and what ensemble or verification strategies yield the most reliable results?
available_evidence: Prompt family effect: CoT +55% commitment, zero-shot +21-24%, few-shot +36%
Coefficient of variation across prompts: 38.2%
Language x prompt interaction
partial_evidence: Per-document commitment variance: BEST-SR CoT=100% vs ZS=43%
needed_evidence: Balanced model x prompt x document matrix
research_question_explanations.interpretation: Stability analysis shows prompt sensitivity; balanced model x prompt x document coverage is needed before ensemble claims are strong.
